title: Bṛhatsaṃhitā 2.14 — Varāhamihira on the standing of the Yavanas: an Indian intellectual judging the Mediterranean rather than trading with it
language_note:
Sanskrit, and the corpus's first. South Asia held ONE record in a language of the region — southasia-01-akananuru-149, Old Tamil — against a Greek periplus and an Egyptian papyrus (FINDING 62); this is the second, and it is in the region's learned language.

BOTH SCRIPTS ARE CARRIED because the two are not interchangeable for this record. The Devanagari is the text; the IAST is a transliteration of it and uses ASCII substitutes where the Devanagari uses its own marks — `|` and `||` for the danda । and double danda ॥ U+0964/U+0965, `14` for the Devanagari digits १४, and U+0027 APOSTROPHE for the avagraha ऽ U+093D in te'pi.

THAT LAST ONE IS DECLARED BECAUSE A FUTURE SESSION WILL OTHERWISE REPAIR IT. U+0027 is exactly the character FINDING 48 measured a fetch substituting for U+2019, and it appears here for an entirely different and correct reason: it is the standard IAST rendering of the avagraha. It is not damage and it must not be normalised to U+2019.
date: c. 550 CE. Varāhamihira's floruit; the Bṛhatsaṃhitā is conventionally placed in the middle of the sixth century. Not derived here.

The Devanagari was never shown and this paste is the first reading of it.

EDITORIAL ACTS, DECLARED. The two register headings are supplied by this record. The verse's own line break between pādas is kept. Nothing else is altered.

WHAT WAS CHECKED BEFORE THE RECORD WAS WRITTEN, AND IT PASSED. The Devanagari carries a correct avagraha ऽ U+093D, danda । U+0964, double danda ॥ U+0965, Devanagari digits १४, and the anusvāra, visarga and virāma signs, all as precomposed NFC with no conjunct damage — which is the failure mode a browser copy of Devanagari usually produces. यवन is present, which is the check that this is doc1218183 = 2.14 and not doc1218184 = 2.15, a verse containing neither yavana nor mleccha and which the hunt's first report gave as the URL.

THE VERSE NUMBER, WHICH IS THE TRAP THIS RECORD IS MOST LIKELY TO BE ACCUSED OF FALLING INTO. The Sanskrit numbers this verse ॥ १४ ॥ and Subrahmanya Sastri & Bhat number it II.14, agreeing with it. IYER NUMBERS THE SAME SENTENCE VERSE 15. Cite as Bṛhatsaṃhitā 2.14 (= Iyer ch. 2 v. 15) with the offset stated, or a reviewer comparing the two open sources will read this record as misattributed.

ONE THING SEEN AND DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED. The Subrahmanya Sastri & Bhat page prints the same verse in Devanagari above its translation, with the same number ॥१४॥. THIS RECORD DOES NOT TRANSCRIBE IT and does not claim it is identical to Jhā's. At the resolution available, ONE AKṢARA — the one Jhā gives as त्ते in ऋषिवत्तेऽपि — could not be resolved against the scan, and a variant is neither asserted nor excluded. A collation of the two Devanagari texts is owed and is a job for somebody with the volume open, not for a reading of a screenshot. FINDING 55.
reference_translation:
N. CHIDAMBARAM IYER, 1884, numbering the verse ch. 2 v. 15
15. Even the Mlecchas and the Yavanas (Greeks) who have well-studied the science are respected as Ṛṣis. Such being the case, if the Jyotiṣaka should happen to be a Brāhmin, who will deny him respect?

V. SUBRAHMANYA SASTRI & M. RAMAKRISHNA BHAT, 1946, numbering it Adhyāya II śloka 14, p. 19
Sloka 14.—The Yavanas are of low origin. When this science has come to stay with them and when such astrologers are worshipped as sages, how much more should an astrologer of the Brahmin origin be ?

TWO PUBLISHED TRANSLATIONS CONSTRUE THE SAME SIX WORDS INCOMPATIBLY, AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS ABOUT HOW TO READ THE SANSKRIT AND NOT ABOUT HOW TO RENDER IT. The words are mlecchā hi yavanāsteṣu. On Iyer's reading they are TWO GROUPS coordinated — 'the Mlecchas AND the Yavanas' — so Varāhamihira lists barbarians alongside Greeks and says both are honoured when learned. On Subrahmanya Sastri & Bhat's reading mlecchāḥ is PREDICATED OF the Yavanas — 'the Yavanas are of low origin' — so Varāhamihira concedes that the Greeks ARE the barbarians and honours them anyway. A list against a predication, on the same unemended text.

THE READING IS UNCERTAIN AND THE VERSE NUMBER TRAVELS WITH IT AS ONE EDITORIAL SPLIT: the translation that reads a list also numbers the verse 15, and the translation that reads a predication numbers it 14 with the Sanskrit.

AND THE TWO AGREE ON THE SECOND HALF, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE DIVERGENCE PRECISE RATHER THAN TOTAL. Both render the a fortiori conclusion — kiṃ punar daivavid dvijaḥ — the same way: Iyer as 'if the Jyotiṣaka should happen to be a Brāhmin, who will deny him respect?' and Sastri & Bhat as 'how much more should an astrologer of the Brahmin origin be?'. The dispute is localised to the first clause. F5_CANDIDATES.md's version of Iyer stopped before this sentence and so could not show the agreement; it is here because a curator read the page to the end.
reference_translation_note:
TWO PUBLISHED TRANSLATIONS, AND THEY REACHED THIS RECORD BY TWO DIFFERENT PATHS THAT ARE NOT EQUALLY GOOD.

THE HUNT'S QUOTATIONS, CHECKED AGAINST THE PAGES. Subrahmanya Sastri & Bhat as F5_CANDIDATES.md carries it is VERBATIM CORRECT. Iyer as it carries him is TRUNCATED — it stops at 'are respected as Ṛṣis.' and drops the sentence that follows, which is the half the two translations agree on.

citation_original:
THREE SOURCES, THREE DIFFERENT RIGHTS POSITIONS, AND NONE OF THEM IS A CLEAN OPEN LICENCE. Recorded under RULING 74, whose third condition is that a record states the position in the source's own terms and, where a source states none, says THAT.

1. WISDOMLIB, for the Devanagari and for Iyer. NO LICENCE IS LISTED. The site states that it is 'free to read online' and offers nothing further. F5_CANDIDATES.md records it as carrying 'no copyright or licence statement of any kind — checked'; that is very nearly right and is refined here — there is a free-to-read statement, which is a weak terms statement rather than none at all.

2. archive.org item VarahamihirasBrihatSamhitaByVSubrahmanyaSastri, for Subrahmanya Sastri & Bhat. THE ITEM CARRIES NO USAGE OR RIGHTS FIELD AT ALL — checked on the item page, where a rights field would sit and where the Mojmal item, for comparison, carries 'Public Domain Mark 1.0'. It is a USER UPLOAD in the `opensource` collection, added 2016-09-15 by the Internet Archive HTML5 Uploader, with no publisher, year or ISBN in its metadata. THE UNDERLYING BOOK IS 1946 AND ITS COPYRIGHT STATUS IS NOT ESTABLISHED BY ANYTHING THIS PROJECT READ.

AND THAT CORRECTS THE HUNT ON A POINT IT GOT SUBTLY WRONG. F5_CANDIDATES.md says 'Cite archive.org and not the blog: both books also circulate as unauthorised uploads on astrofoxx.wordpress.com', which reads as though archive.org were the authorised home. IT IS ITSELF A USER UPLOAD WITH NO RIGHTS STATEMENT. Citing it rather than the blog is an improvement in DURABILITY AND TRACEABILITY — a stable identifier, an ark, page images at 600 ppi — and not an improvement in rights. The record cites it for the first reason and says so.

3. Iyer 1884 is genuinely out of copyright and its archive.org scan is recorded by the hunt as CC0. That one is clean.

A PUBLIC-DOMAIN SECOND WITNESS TO THE SANSKRIT EXISTS AND WAS NOT USED: H. Kern, The Bṛhat Sañhitā of Varāha-Mihira (Calcutta: Baptist Mission Press, 1865), archive.org/details/bhatsahitavarha00kerngoog, NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT. Collating Jhā's Devanagari against Kern's would give this record a second witness to its source text — the thing eastasia-07-tang-huiyao has and almost nothing else in this corpus does — and it is owed rather than done. KERN'S OWN ENGLISH IS NOT ON ARCHIVE.ORG: that item is his SANSKRIT edition. His translation is serialised across JRAS n.s. IV–VII (1870–75), abstract-only on Cambridge Core. Two hunts have now looked.
notes:
F5 Part 3, record 40, and F5's South Asia verbatim_with_provenance slot.

WHAT IT SAYS ABOUT ROME, AND IT IS THE ONLY RECORD IN THIS CORPUS THAT SAYS IT. Every other record here is contact — an embassy, a cargo, a coin, a hoard, a dedication. THIS ONE IS A JUDGEMENT. Varāhamihira, laying down who may be trusted to practise astral science, has to account for the fact that the science reached India from the Greek-speaking Mediterranean, and he does it in one verse: the Yavanas stand where they stand, the science is soundly established among them, and they are honoured like ṛṣis for it — so how much more the twice-born who knows it. An Indian intellectual placing the Mediterranean in a hierarchy rather than trading with it, and conceding its learning while keeping its rank.

GLOSS-CAPABLE, contested_reading. Two published translations, both open, both read at the page, construing mlecchā hi yavanāsteṣu as a list and as a predication. THE MECHANICAL REQUIREMENT IS MET: both translations and the statement of what is uncertain sit inside reference_translation, which the loader chunks, and none of it is in notes, which it does not. AND THE RULE THAT KILLED THE LIANGSHU'S SECOND READING IS SATISFIED: neither alternative is this project's. Both are published, both are citable, and the record supplies nothing of its own.

THE HONESTY NOTE, CARRIED FORWARD FROM F5 PART 2 AND NOT SOFTENED. Part 2 broke the capture rule on this record — not with a fetch, which stayed silent, but in a progress message to the curator which QUOTED BOTH ENGLISH RENDERINGS. The curator's paste of the two translations is therefore A CONFIRMATION AND NOT AN INDEPENDENT SECOND READING, and this record says so where a reader will meet it. The Devanagari was never shown and its capture is genuinely blind. The rule as written guards the locating fetch; nothing guarded the session's own summaries back to the curator, and that is where it went.

AND THIS SESSION ADDED A SECOND, SMALLER BREACH OF THE SAME KIND, RECORDED FOR THE SAME REASON AND SINCE RETIRED. Subrahmanya Sastri & Bhat arrived as a page image and was TRANSCRIBED BY THE MODEL rather than typed by the curator. The capture rule exists so that the model is not the transcriber. THE CURATOR CONFIRMED IT INDEPENDENTLY ON 2026-09-05 and the two readings agree character for character across all 188 characters of the sentence; see reference_translation_note, where the one element the confirmation does NOT cover is named.

THE CORRECTION THIS CAPTURE MADE TO THE HUNT. F5_CANDIDATES.md quotes Iyer as ending at 'are respected as Ṛṣis.' The page continues, and the continuation is the sentence in which Iyer and Sastri & Bhat AGREE. The truncated quotation made the divergence look total when it is localised to the first clause — and a localised divergence is the better contested reading, because it isolates exactly which words are construed two ways. SEVENTH DOCUMENT CORRECTION OF THIS SESSION, and the fourth in which the half after the cut was the half that mattered.

THE BOUNDARY. Kern's 1865 Sanskrit was not collated against Jhā's; the two Devanagari texts have not been compared and one akṣara of the Sastri & Bhat printing could not be resolved from a screenshot. Bhat's 1981 Motilal Banarsidass revision is print-only and was not consulted. Kern's own English is paywalled in JRAS. The Bhaṭṭotpala commentary on this very verse is the subject of a separate record in this tranche and the two sit on the same six words — declared in advance as a retrieval-crowding risk for the ranking run, which `beaten_by` can now see.

subject_places.name: the Yavanas (यवन, yavana)
subject_places.note:
The Greek-speaking Mediterranean world as Sanskrit names it, and the only place-like entity the verse names. `mentioned` and NOT a directional role: the verse says where the Yavanas stand in a hierarchy and that the science is established among them — it describes no movement, and the movement a reader knows about (Greek astral science reaching India) IS NOT IN THIS TEXT. A block of nothing but `mentioned` needs no focus and PLACES.md is explicit that it must not be made to invent one.

NO GAZETTEER ID, AND ONE WAS LOOKED FOR. The pinned 2026-08-10 Pleiades dump holds no place titled Yavana, Yona, Ionia, Iones or Ionians. The corpus places a people WITH an id only where the gazetteer holds that ethnonym as a place with an extent — arabia-05-ruwafa's Thamudaei at Pleiades 814740 — and WITHOUT one otherwise, as eastasia-07-tang-huiyao's Dashi and persia-05-abnun's Hrōmāy. This is the second kind.

THE MLECCHAS ARE NOT PLACED, AND THAT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. Whether the verse names them as a SECOND group at all is precisely what the two published translations disagree about — see reference_translation. Placing them would settle by keystroke a question this record exists to hold open.
